findings.title: Decline, darkness, and witnessed dawn
findings.claim: The focus schedule runs from solar decline through night darkness and singles out dawn recitation as witnessed; 17:79 adds a night vigil by the preceding text, while 17:96 names divine witness at the pericope close. The ordered context changes the time list into devotional practice across light transitions, with dawn recitation held in both attendance and attestation.
findings.mechanism: The focus carries solar movement, night darkening, the Qur'an of dawn, and a witnessed predicate. The immediate continuation repeats night as the setting of an additional vigil and appears to carry the focus recitation through its pronoun; the close repeats witnessing in a statement of divine sufficiency. These contacts extend the interval into night practice and let the focus witness meet a second, testimonial frame.
findings.reader_payoff: The time marks appear as a lived rhythm across decline, darkness, night vigil, and dawn, while the recitation remains witnessed without requiring one specified audience.
findings.containment: The focus remains the command to establish prayer in its stated span and the assertion that dawn recitation is witnessed. The night vigil is a distinct added practice. The pronoun in 17:79 is only qualifiedly linked to the preceding Qur'an, and 17:96 does not grammatically identify the witnesses of 17:78.
